checks.invariant: exec uses _Head streaming byte cap and _timed, while list_dir, outbox_list, and exists/is_dir are checked for container-side timeouts and output byte caps
checks.result: Confirmed from source that exec streams through _Head with _OUT_LIMIT (64 KiB) and _timed(t), read_file and outbox_read use head -c and _timed(_READ_TIMEOUT), workspace_manifest uses head -c and _timed(_MANIFEST_TIMEOUT). However, list_dir and outbox_list use c.exec_run without _timed or head byte caps, buffering arbitrary output in control-plane memory.

checks.invariant: preview_command glob expansion and recursive directory walking enforce call bounds and output record caps
checks.result: Sandboxed test confirmed that preview_command enforces PREVIEW_CALLS_MAX (40) and truncates affected items to limit (200), and _walk uses head -z; however, _expand has no record or byte cap, allowing wildcards matching thousands of paths to buffer full output before truncation.

checks.invariant: desktop_processes and screenshot enforce timeouts and output buffering bounds
checks.result: desktop_processes uses _timed(_X_TIMEOUT) with ps -eo bounded by container pids_limit (1024), and screenshot uses _timed(_X_TIMEOUT) with scrot -o -z, though screenshot cats the entire PNG into memory without streaming byte cap.

checks.invariant: list_dir and outbox_list callers propagate uncurbed container output to control-plane consumers
checks.result: Confirmed that api.py /sandboxes/{sid}/outbox and web.py outbox_frag pass outbox_list output directly to JSON serialization and Jinja template rendering without pagination or cardinality bounds, and service.py _call_tool routes list_dir directly to the container.

checks.invariant: AgentBox.disk_low accurately accounts for all host disk growth vectors caused by agent actions
checks.result: Sandboxed test and source inspection established that disk_low queries only shutil.disk_usage(s.db_path.parent).free against min_free_bytes; when container layers or Docker images grow outside db_path.parent, disk_low remains False and does not trip the 507 guard.

checks.invariant: container writable layers and snapshot images are bounded by filesystem quotas and deployment volume layout
checks.result: Confirmed that config.disk_limit defaults to empty string so sandbox._run_container omits storage_opt, leaving container layers without size quotas, and snapshot commits images to Docker storage root up to snapshot_quota (50) per sandbox across unlimited sandboxes, while deploy/docker-compose.yml mounts AGENTBOX_HOME separately from the host Docker storage root.

candidates.title: Unbounded buffering and missing container-side timeouts in list_dir, outbox_list, and preview glob expand
candidates.description: While exec streams output through _Head (capping memory to 64 KiB) and read_file, outbox_read, and workspace_manifest apply container-side head caps and timeouts, list_dir and outbox_list invoke c.exec_run without container-side _timed timeouts or stream-limiting byte caps, buffering arbitrary output in the control-plane process. Furthermore, preview _expand lacks output cardinality/byte limits, allowing an agent with a populated workspace or outbox to exhaust control-plane RAM or block worker threads indefinitely.
candidates.claimed_root_cause: Container output consumption disciplines were applied inconsistently: exec uses _Head streaming (_OUT_LIMIT=64 KiB) and _timed, read_file/outbox_read use head -c and _timed, workspace_manifest uses head -c and _timed, and preview _walk uses head -z and _timed. However, list_dir (ls -la) and outbox_list (find -printf) lack both container-side timeouts and output byte bounds, while preview _expand has a 10s timeout but no output byte cap or record limit. An agent-populated directory with hundreds of thousands of files causes c.exec_run to buffer all demuxed bytes in memory, parse them into unbounded Python structures, and potentially stall tool_pool and HTTP worker threads.

trace.description: Agent calls list_dir or triggers approval preview (via exec) on an agent-populated directory, or human views outbox via GET /sandboxes/{sid}/outbox.
list_dir calls c.exec_run(["ls", "-la", "--", p], demux=True) without _timed and without _Head streaming, waiting for all container output to buffer into control-plane RAM.
outbox_list executes find without _timed or head cap, passing raw output to _parse_outbox which instantiates uncurbed Python lists of dicts.
Control plane process buffers unbounded byte arrays and creates thousands of Python objects, risking memory exhaustion in the 2 GB control container or threadpool worker exhaustion.

evidence.description: exec streams output into _Head with _OUT_LIMIT cap and _timed(t, kill_after=5).
list_dir runs c.exec_run(["ls", "-la", "--", p]) with no _timed timeout and no byte cap.
outbox_list runs c.exec_run with find -printf without _timed or output truncation before _parse_outbox.
_expand runs container glob without head -z or output limit, unlike _walk which uses head -z.

blockers: Demonstrating full control-plane memory exhaustion or threadpool hang under large-scale container output requires running against a live Docker daemon with a real container, which is excluded from the subagent sandbox environment.

validation_plan.local: In a live test with Docker running: (1) create a sandbox container, (2) populate /workspace/outbox with 200,000 files using a fast shell loop, (3) call GET /sandboxes/{sid}/outbox and POST /sandboxes/{sid}/tools/list_dir with path /workspace/outbox, (4) observe control plane memory consumption spike and monitor process RSS; (5) test replacing outbox with a hanging device or slow pipe to observe thread starvation.
validation_plan.deployment: Review production control-plane logs and metrics under high file counts for OOM kills (mem_limit: 2g) or 504/timeout errors on list_dir and outbox endpoints.

candidates.title: disk_low measures SQLite db_path.parent rather than Docker daemon storage root allowing complete host disk exhaustion
candidates.description: AgentBox.disk_low checks free disk space strictly via shutil.disk_usage(self.settings.db_path.parent). In deployments where the agentbox database volume (AGENTBOX_HOME) and Docker's data root (/var/lib/docker) reside on separate filesystems, container layer growth and docker commit snapshot images (up to 50 per sandbox) consume Docker storage without decreasing free space on db_path.parent. The 507 guard never trips, allowing agents to exhaust host Docker disk, cause daemon failures, and prevent administrative log_human operations which fail closed with 503.
candidates.claimed_root_cause: The disk guard in AgentBox.disk_low (service.py:421-437) assumes all disk growth occurs on the filesystem containing db_path.parent. However, Docker container writable layers and commit images (sandbox.py:356-370) grow inside Docker's data root (e.g. /var/lib/docker). In deploy/docker-compose.yml, AGENTBOX_HOME (/var/lib/agentbox) is a separate bind mount. When db_path.parent and Docker data root are on distinct partitions, or when an admitted exec runs dd/fallocate for up to exec_timeout (since AGENTBOX_DISK is empty by default so containers have no storage_opt size quota), host Docker storage can be completely filled without triggering disk_low.

trace.description: Agent calls an admitted tool (e.g. exec writing large files to /workspace, or write_file triggering snapshot).

disk_low evaluates shutil.disk_usage(s.db_path.parent).free against s.min_free_bytes; because Docker storage is on a separate filesystem, db_path.parent free space remains high and disk_low returns False.
c.commit commits container writable layer into a new Docker image in Docker data root, accumulating up to snapshot_quota (50) images per sandbox.
Container has no storage_opt disk quota (disk_limit is empty by default), allowing unrestricted accumulation of data in Docker's storage root until the host filesystem is exhausted.

evidence.description: disk_limit defaults to empty string, disabling container storage_opt size limits.
snapshot_quota defaults to 50 snapshots per sandbox without aggregate disk quota.
snapshot calls c.commit(), creating full container layer image copies in Docker root.
AGENTBOX_HOME is mounted to /var/lib/agentbox separately from Docker host root.

blockers: Simulating separate filesystem mounts for AGENTBOX_HOME and Docker root (/var/lib/docker) along with live docker commit image accumulation requires access to a host Docker daemon and multiple mount points, which is unavailable in the isolated sandbox.

validation_plan.local: On a live host running Docker with AGENTBOX_HOME on a loopback mount or separate partition from /var/lib/docker: (1) configure min_free_bytes=256MB, (2) run an agent script that creates files and commits snapshots up to snapshot_quota, (3) verify that disk_low continues returning False while Docker data root disk usage increases until /var/lib/docker is exhausted.
validation_plan.deployment: Check host partition layout in production deployments to verify whether /var/lib/docker and AGENTBOX_HOME are on separate volumes, and monitor Docker daemon root volume free space independently of the application database volume.

hardening: agentbox/sandbox.py:list_dir-and-outbox_list: Wrap ls -la in list_dir and find in outbox_list with _timed(_READ_TIMEOUT) to prevent hung container filesystems from holding tool_pool or HTTP request worker threads indefinitely.

agentbox/sandbox.py:_expand-head-limit: Add a head -z limit to _expand in sandbox.py similar to _walk's head -z -n "$2" to cap the number of glob-expanded path strings returned before control-plane parsing.

agentbox/service.py:disk_low-docker-root: Query the Docker daemon storage root filesystem or enforce mandatory AGENTBOX_DISK container quotas so that disk_low accounts for container layer and snapshot growth.
